subject: How to trim the first methylated C by end repairing for RRBS data

messages.author: 9da0a58949b5e955
messages.subject: How to trim the first methylated C by end repairing for RRBS data
parts:
My problem is how can I trim the first C in methylation calling, when I am dealing with RRBS data with non-strand specific sequencing and end repairing by methylated C.
The alignment result by bismark looks like this:

HWI-ST926:366:C4CUVACXX:1:1201:6554:17343_1:N:0:CGATGT  16      chr1    10497   255     50M     *       0       0 CGAATCTAACCTAAAAAAAACTATACTCCGCCTTCAAAATACCACCGAAA      CCCFFBB=DDFDDHHHGHJJJJJJJGHHIJGIIJJIIJJICBBHHHB;BE      NM:i:11 MD:Z:2G0G3G4G1G0G1G4G1G11G1G11  XM:Z:.Zxh...x....x.hh.h....x.h....Z......x.h.......Z... XR:Z:GA XG:Z:GA


Thank you.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How to trim the first methylated C by end repairing for RRBS data
parts:
You can use bismark methylation extractor in bedgraph format to ignore arbitrary number of bases. You may need a lot of memory when using that (they may have improved it lately).

also see this thread:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/methylkit_discussion/bismark$20bedgraph/methylkit_discussion/ZtCjWLYlW-w/cE5_1Y_cRxMJ

Best,
ALtuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How to trim the first methylated C by end repairing for RRBS data
parts:
I think you can read them in as all + or - strand, then use unite() with destrand=FALSE, and keep in mind strand information is incorrect for some bases, I don't think it will cause any problems but there might be a problem I can not foresee. 

You can also assign pseudo strand to Cs on the CpG context. For example 12284 must be + and 12285 must be -, because they are adjacent and I'm assuming your file has CpG context. You can get location of all Cs in CpG context using BSgenome package (should be about 23M for human) and assign + strand to positions which match the coordinates in your files, and the rest - strand. Then you can even use unite with destrand=TRUE.


Best,
Altuna
